title: Runtime, port and debugger maintenance
summary: Review eight material upstream changes spanning a new native Saturn output, source-only release validation, decompilation semantics, emulator/debugger correctness and reverse-engineering instrumentation.
notes: The CPU audit queue returned zero unresolved source or target CPU areas. SH-2 was added only for the explicit gcc-sh-elf -m2 Saturn output. No minimum hardware was inferred, and no upstream program, ROM, image, build or test suite was executed by the tracker.

project.display_title: Mega Man X4 decompilation — PlayStation, Linux & Saturn
project.status: Active multi-platform decompilation: current CI builds the PlayStation variants, Linux ports and a native Sega Saturn SH-2 image; runtime/playability not independently tested

identity.narrative: US executable reconstruction with typed engine/gameplay C and original-file extraction requirements. ROM/executable matching and completeness not independently tested.

classification.narrative: The project remains a Mega Man X4 decompilation and now also carries native Linux and Sega Saturn output paths; the Saturn path is a port, not evidence that the original PlayStation executable used SH-2.

target_cpu.narrative: The existing PlayStation output remains MIPS. The new Saturn-native manifest and assembly compile with gcc-sh-elf using -m2, explicitly establishing SH-2 as an additional output CPU.

build.narrative: GitHub Actions completed the PlayStation, Linux and new `Build Saturn with GCC` jobs successfully for the reviewed commit. This supports compilable=true as an upstream CI result.
build.limitations: The tracker did not compile, execute or play any build, and CI success does not establish runtime completeness or byte identity.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The Saturn job creates a no-disc image, but the reviewed change and successful CI check do not establish a runnable-hardware test, minimum RAM, chipset revision or other minimum hardware profile.

ai.narrative: The reviewed commit contains no development-AI attribution; absence in this bounded commit is not proof of non-use.

relationships.narrative: Screened URL, title and prior decisions. GitHub fork flag is not treated as conclusive lineage evidence.

project.status: Active source-only v1.9.2 native Mega Drive port; fixes early-hit boss invulnerability and wrapped Round 3 arena arrivals

identity.narrative: Root README, manifest and repository metadata identify a source-only Black Tiger arcade-to-Mega Drive port. The manifest says the exact revision is unknown despite hash-locked files; do not silently claim an independently verified arcade revision.

classification.narrative: v1.9.2 remains a native SGDK/Mega Drive behavioral port. The release text explicitly says the cartridge does not execute the arcade CPU, so the update is not relabelled as embedded emulation or original-source recovery.

source_cpu.narrative: Z80 established by player audit and MAME primary driver, which identifies main and audio Z80 CPUs. Driver also describes an 8751 protection MCU; the reviewed port scope reconstructs Z80 gameplay/audio behavior, not that MCU's program.

target_cpu.narrative: README explicitly states native 68000 game logic; Makefile invokes m68k-elf-gcc -m68000. No inferred host CPU.

build.narrative: Upstream reports all 191 Makefile test recipes and strict packaging passing, with controlled boss fixtures plus Genesis Plus GX and isolated PicoDrive smoke tests for the final 4 MiB ROM.
build.limitations: No local build, emulator run, natural full playthrough or physical-hardware retest was performed; the repository remains source-only and supplies no public release binary.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The release cites emulator checks and an earlier user report involving a Mega Drive Model 2 VA0 and EverGenesis V3, but explicitly says those physical configurations were unavailable for retest. No minimum hardware profile is recorded.

ai.narrative: The reviewed release commit contains no development-AI attribution; absence in this bounded evidence is not proof of non-use.

relationships.narrative: Distinct from Side Arms MD; shares author/SGDK/native-port approach. MAME is an offline reference/oracle, not runtime. No canonical or subject duplicate in catalogue.

project.status: Active GBA decompilation; current source names room-script actor operations, turn-key handling, hit results and the intro sweep flip

identity.narrative: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban — GBA decompilation. Repository root and implementation inspected at pinned revisions.

classification.narrative: The reviewed change advances semantic recovery inside the existing GBA decompilation by replacing generic actor-animation labels with tile-actor route/stop operations and naming additional gameplay and presentation behavior.

source_cpu.narrative: Architecture context: arm. Source and target roles are recorded separately.

build.narrative: The repository's deploy check completed successfully for the reviewed commit, supporting continued generated-output publication while not proving a complete or independently reproduced game build.
build.limitations: The tracker did not compile, run or compare the candidate ROM.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Owned international and Japanese ROMs required; Linux/WSL toolchain. Raw art assets not included.

ai.narrative: The reviewed commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5 as co-author. This confirms AI contribution for this commit only and does not generalize authorship across the project.

relationships.narrative: Credits speedrunning researchers, Krawall LGPL engine and Pucrunch algorithm; third-party library source is not newly reversed game code.

project.status: Active Hyper Neo Geo 64 SDK; current tools add MAME instrumentation for MIPS/IOMCU command-response analysis

identity.narrative: Very early native Hyper Neo Geo 64 SDK with MIPS startup/vector setup, TLB/core initialization, linker/build rules and an implemented Go ELF-to-cartridge ROM packer. The empty sample is only an example of the reusable SDK, not a separate game.

classification.narrative: The repository remains an original Hyper Neo Geo 64 development kit. The new iomcutap.lua is directly relevant reverse-engineering instrumentation, but it does not turn the SDK itself into a reconstructed commercial game.

source_cpu.narrative: Authored native homebrew/SDK; no separately recovered predecessor source architecture.

target_cpu.narrative: Native build and implementation establish output architecture; compiler host is separate.

build.narrative: The new Lua tap records main-CPU commands, I/O-MCU replies, port activity, events and EEPROM traffic through MAME's scripting API for behavioral analysis.
build.limitations: The tracker did not run MAME, supply ROMs or capture a tap log.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Author explicitly reports testing only on MAME. External HNG64 BIOS is required. roadedge naming is a MAME packaging workaround and does not make this a Road Edge game port or CPU wrapper. No real-hardware claim.

ai.narrative: The reviewed commit contains no development-AI attribution; absence in this bounded evidence is not proof of non-use.

relationships.narrative: Targets HNG64 native code; Linux/Docker and Go are host tooling. No binary predecessor or source architecture is assigned to this authored SDK.

project.status: Active Sharp MZ emulator/debugger; MCP breakpoint names now persist, ignored DD/FD prefixes are modeled explicitly, and MZF size checks handle unreadable files

identity.narrative: Open-source Sharp MZ emulator with cycle-accurate Z80A execution, chip/peripheral emulation, a built-in debugger and an MCP bridge exposing screenshots, coverage, profiling and analysis controls. Primary docs provide Linux, Windows and macOS build paths; no minimum host CPU or RAM is stated. Claude client configuration documents a supported integration, not evidence that AI authored the project. Current main saves hidden Z80 MEMPTR, interrupt, EI-delay and T-state state plus CTC, scroll, VRAM-wait and floppy-controller state; it safely adapts RAMdisk/IDE8 snapshot loads. Debugger/MCP fixes expose all 532 expanded memory regions, keep debugger reads from firing guest watchpoints, correctly stop temporary run-to breakpoints and record the instruction bytes actually fetched by self-modifying code. Evidence: https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/commit/1f477d90e2efd6808253c1c3d5f31fa56f465570 https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/commit/a5726b9658d10b4412cf4a28bc212a78351f28a4 Current main adds frame-boundary-synchronized memory search across user RAM, logical Z80 space, VRAM, extension banks, RAM disks and other writable memory, with numeric/string types, filters, undo/redo, candidate actions, freeze controls and write-origin inspection. Matching MCP tools expose searches and freezes for automation, and the same change fixes the missing second half of PEHU 512 KiB memory. A maintained locale catalog at the reviewed commit explicitly names Claude Code as Last-Translator, correcting the prior no-evidence AI audit while keeping attribution limited to that content. Evidence: https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/commit/0e4967ca56d162bcd2dc3607ebab986f9e029e78 https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/blob/0e4967ca56d162bcd2dc3607ebab986f9e029e78/src/locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/mz800emu.po

classification.narrative: The current change materially improves debugger semantics and automation: user breakpoint names survive MCP address updates, and ignored DD/FD prefixes are displayed as DD*/FD* rather than mislabelled NOP* instructions.

source_cpu.narrative: README explicitly states cycle-accurate Z80A CPU emulation.

target_cpu.narrative: Host emulator and analysis environment; no fixed emitted target CPU.

build.narrative: The commit adds standalone disassembler-prefix coverage and an MCP end-to-end breakpoint-name test, while guarding MZF size inspection when a file cannot be opened or measured.
build.limitations: The tracker reviewed source and tests but did not build or execute the emulator or test suite.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Host-side emulator; supported host OSes are documented, but no minimum CPU or RAM profile is stated.

ai.narrative: The existing project-level Claude Code attribution remains based on the maintained locale catalogue. The reviewed commit itself adds no new AI attribution, so its authorship is not inferred.

relationships.narrative: README identifies the SourceForge predecessor and the related z80-mz800, TapeMZ and mzdisk projects.

project.status: Work in progress; snapshot saving now coordinates interpreter-linked object memory, garbage-collection roots and host file operations

identity.narrative: Independent implementation of the complete Bluebook Smalltalk-80 VM and environment in Smalltalk itself, with Tonel-format interpreter, object memory, BitBlt, display and filesystem adapters for Pharo.

classification.narrative: The project remains a Pharo-hosted implementation of the Bluebook Smalltalk-80 VM. The current commit deepens VM implementation rather than preserving or decompiling a native historical binary.

source_cpu.narrative: No physical predecessor input architecture established; compiler/VM host CPU is not treated as recovered input.

target_cpu.narrative: No particular physical output CPU established; implementation-language portability does not prove host support.

build.narrative: The snapshot path now links ObjectMemory to the interpreter, preserves active/new-process roots around collection, and adds host file create/delete/close operations used by image persistence.
build.limitations: The tracker did not install Pharo, load the package, save a snapshot or validate image compatibility.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Pharo 11 or newer remains the documented host requirement, but the current change states no minimum CPU, RAM or operating-system version.

ai.narrative: The reviewed commit contains no development-AI attribution; absence in this bounded evidence is not proof of non-use.

relationships.narrative: Credits Banay implementation for debugging reference, Bluebook chapters, and Mario Wolczko image archive.

project.status: Active classic-Mac API runtime; PPC CarbonLib math exports now fall back through MathLib with compatibility tests

identity.narrative: Rust high-level runtime implementing classic Mac Toolbox/OS managers and 68k/PPC application loaders so original Macintosh applications can execute without a Macintosh ROM or installed System.

classification.narrative: Systemless remains a clean high-level classic-Mac API/runtime reimplementation. The current change extends PPC CFM import compatibility rather than introducing recovered Apple system source.

source_cpu.narrative: Documented source/input platforms: Macintosh. Processor scope: m68k, PowerPC.

target_cpu.narrative: Documented output/support targets: macOS, Linux, Windows, Web. Processor scope: ARM64, x86-64, WebAssembly.

build.narrative: When CarbonLib lacks a requested symbol, the PPC loader now resolves supported floating-point entry points through MathLib while retaining InterfaceLib bindings for Toolbox names; regression coverage checks representative symbols.
build.limitations: The tracker did not compile or run the runtime or a Carbon application.

runtime_profiles.narrative: README lists native x86-64 and ARM64 releases, Linux glibc 2.35+ and ALSA runtime. No complete RAM or minimal processor model established.

ai.narrative: Prior reviewed commits explicitly establish Claude contribution to parts of the project. The current commit carries no new AI trailer, so no additional attribution is inferred.

relationships.narrative: 68k and PPC execution cores are Cargo dependencies, while Toolbox/OS manager reimplementation is project-specific. Do not label it original recovered Apple OS source.

project.status: Active Atari 2600 emulator/debugger; terminal command dispatch now avoids a channel deadlock exposed by repeated RELOAD commands

identity.narrative: The reviewed repository remains the existing Gopher2600 — Atari 2600 emulator and debugger project.

classification.narrative: Gopher2600 remains a general Atari 2600 emulator and debugger. The current change corrects debugger command concurrency and does not alter its project identity or introduce a separate tool.

source_cpu.narrative: The retained source CPU decision remains 6507; no architecture is inferred from host language or platform alone.

target_cpu.narrative: Release v0.57.2 explicitly publishes Linux/Windows amd64, macOS Intel and macOS Apple Silicon packages. The record therefore adds x86-64 and arm64 output architectures.

build.narrative: Terminal input is now copied and sent from an ephemeral goroutine so the GUI does not block while the emulation goroutine is waiting for feature-set channel traffic; the commit identifies repeated RELOAD commands as the observable trigger.
build.limitations: The tracker did not build the emulator or reproduce the deadlock.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The existing published x86-64 Linux/Windows and x86-64/arm64 macOS profiles remain unchanged; the concurrency fix states no new minimum hardware requirement.

ai.narrative: The reviewed commit contains no development-AI attribution; absence in this bounded evidence is not proof of non-use.

relationships.narrative: The README identifies Stella as a visual reference and source for CDF/audio/cartridge fingerprints, plus 6502.ts as an audio reference. This is documented reference lineage, not evidence that Gopher2600 is a fork or derived code base.
